evals.expected_output: Should analyze the current project (this refactor plugin — Go-based, with GitHub Actions CI, Makefile, golangci-lint, etc.), detect no existing hook manager, recommend lefthook or pre-commit, present tiered recommendations with rationale tied to what it found in CI, and ask which hooks to install.
expectations: The skill detected the project's primary language(s) by examining package manifests (go.mod, package.json, pyproject.toml, or similar)
The skill checked for existing hook managers (husky, pre-commit, lefthook) and reported whether any were found
The skill examined CI/CD configuration files (e.g., .github/workflows/*.yml) to identify what checks already run remotely
The skill detected existing linter/formatter configurations (e.g., golangci-yml, eslint, ruff, prettier) that are actually configured in the project
The skill organized recommendations into tiers or priority levels based on what it found, not a generic checklist
The skill recommended a specific hook manager appropriate for the detected stack with rationale
The skill asked the user which hooks they want to install rather than silently installing anything
The skill mentioned --no-verify or a bypass mechanism for emergencies

evals.expected_output: Should run full analysis silently, choose a hook manager based on detected stack, select tier 1 + applicable tier 2 hooks automatically, then display exactly what would be written without writing anything. Should include file paths and configuration content.
expectations: The skill did NOT ask the user any interactive questions (auto mode skips elicitation)
The skill did NOT write or create any hook configuration files (dry-run mode)
The skill displayed the specific file paths that would be created or modified
The skill showed the actual configuration content that would be written (not just descriptions)
The skill selected a hook manager appropriate for the detected project stack
The skill selected hooks based on detected tooling — only recommending tools that are already configured in the project

evals.prompt: I keep getting CI failures because I forget to run the linter before pushing. Can you set up something to catch that?
evals.expected_output: Should trigger the git-hooks skill, analyze the project to find the specific linter and CI lint step, then propose a pre-commit hook that runs that linter on staged files. Should reference the actual CI config it found.
expectations: The skill identified the specific linter tool configured in the project (not a generic recommendation)
The skill examined CI configuration to find the lint step and referenced it specifically
The skill proposed a pre-commit or pre-push hook that runs the detected linter on staged/changed files only (not the entire repo)
The skill explained how the proposed hook would prevent the CI failures the user described
The skill mentioned the estimated execution time or addressed speed concerns for the proposed hook
